primary.title: My Life and Work
primary.author: Henry Ford
primary.rationale: Autobiographical account of Ford's life, philosophy, and business practices. Widely available and influential.

primary.title: The Dearborn Independent
primary.author: Henry Ford
primary.rationale: A newspaper published by Ford, which contained many of his views and opinions, including controversial ones. While individual articles are hard to cite, the publication itself is a primary source.

primary.title: Moving Forward
primary.author: Henry Ford
primary.rationale: A later work by Ford, reflecting on his experiences and outlook on industry and society.

secondary.title: The Machine in the Garden: Technology and the Pastoral Ideal in America
secondary.author: Leo Marx
secondary.rationale: Although published before 1976, this seminal work discusses the impact of industrialization, with significant attention to figures like Ford and the automobile's role in shaping American landscapes and ideals. It provides crucial context for understanding Ford's legacy.

secondary.title: Henry Ford: A Biography
secondary.author: Peter Collier
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive biography that offers scholarly analysis of Ford's life, business, and impact.

secondary.title: The American Automobile: A Diversified History
secondary.author: Michael L. Berger
secondary.rationale: This book likely places Henry Ford within the broader context of the American automotive industry, offering scholarly analysis of his contributions and influence.

suggestions.notes: Henry Ford's primary writings, particularly 'My Life and Work,' are readily available. Secondary sources should focus on scholarly biographies and histories of the automobile industry and American industrialization.
